records.central_bank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
records.people: Jasmina Selimovic (member of the CBBH Governing Board from 3 January 2024; Governor and chair of the Governing Board)
records.move: from independent member of the Supervisory Board of Raiffeisen Bank BiH (2018) to member of the CBBH Governing Board (January 2024) and Governor ; from president of the Board of Directors of the Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance (since 2021) to the CBBH Governing Board
records.summary: The central bank's own profile page gives her career in order: employed at the Faculty of Economics in Sarajevo since 2004, where she is a full professor and was elected Dean in 2018 with a second four-year mandate in 2022; member of the Advisory Group of the Fiscal Council of Bosnia and Herzegovina 2011-2015, representing the Prime Minister of the Federation of BiH; independent member of the Supervisory Board of Raiffeisen Bank BiH in 2018; president of the Board of Directors of the Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance since 2021; and appointed by the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the CBBH Governing Board on 3 January 2024 for a six-year mandate. The CBBH page does not say who owns Raiffeisen Bank BiH. The bank's own ownership page (https://www.raiffeisenbank.ba/en/about-us/about-raiffeisen/who-we-are/raiffeisen-bosna-i-hercegovina.html) lists a single owner, Raiffeisen SEE Region Holding GmbH at 100.00%, with no state shareholder, so the employer is privately owned; the page itself does not use the words private or commercial. The Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance is a statutory public body, and the Fiscal Council role was a government appointment.
records.source_title: Jasmina Selimovic, Governor and Chairman of the Governing Board (Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina)

records.people: Ibrahim L. Stevens (Director of Research 2008-2010, Deputy Governor from July 2014, First Deputy Governor, Governor since November 2023)
records.move: from a decade at the Bank of England, including Senior Adviser at its Centre for Central Banking Studies, to Director of Research at the Bank of Sierra Leone (2008-2010, on secondment from the Bank of England) ; from Country Programme Director at the International Growth Centre at the London School of Economics and macroeconomic adviser to Rwanda's Ministry of Finance under a GIZ-funded project to Deputy Governor (July 2014) and Governor (November 2023)
records.summary: This biography page sets out his career as printed. He spent a decade at the Bank of England, including a post as Senior Adviser at the Bank's Centre for Central Banking Studies, with no start or end dates given. He was appointed Director of Research at the Bank of Sierra Leone from 2008 to 2010, during which he was seconded from the Bank of England. The page also lists, without dates, roles as Country Programme Director at the International Growth Centre at the London School of Economics, Macroeconomic Adviser to the Ministry of Finance and Economic Development in Rwanda, and Head of Project for a German International Cooperation (GIZ) funded initiative on macroeconomic advice to Rwanda, plus academic posts at Durham University and Queen Mary University of London. He was appointed Deputy Governor in July 2014, reappointed for a second five-year term in 2019, became First Deputy Governor after the Bank of Sierra Leone Act 2019, and has been Governor since November 2023. Every outside employer named is public or academic: the Bank of England is a central bank, GIZ is a German state development agency, the Rwandan ministry is a government body, and the IGC sits within the London School of Economics. The page names no private employer.
records.source_title: Ibrahim L. Stevens (Africa Finance and Trade Initiative, George Washington University)

records.people: Gobind Ganga (Director of Research 1995-November 2003, Deputy Governor from June 2005, Governor from 2 December 2014)
records.move: from Director of Research at the Bank of Guyana to Alternate Executive Director at the World Bank in Washington DC (November 2003) ; from the World Bank back to the Bank of Guyana as Deputy Governor (appointed June 2005) and Governor (2 December 2014)
records.summary: The Bank of Guyana's own profile of the Governor gives the career in order. He took a BA at the University of Winnipeg and an MA and PhD in Economics at the University of Manitoba during the 1980s, then held academic posts: lecturer and senior research fellow at his alma mater, lecturer in economics at the University of the West Indies, Mona Campus in Jamaica, adjunct professor at the Consortium Graduate School at Mona, and senior researcher and senior lecturer at the University of Guyana, Turkeyen Campus. In 1995 he was appointed Director of the Research Department at the Bank of Guyana, a post he held until November 2003, when he was appointed Alternate Executive Director at the World Bank in Washington DC, representing ten Caribbean territories together with Canada and Ireland. In June 2005 he was appointed Deputy Governor at the Bank of Guyana, taking up the role after completing his World Bank term, and on 2 December 2014 he was appointed Governor. The page also records service since 1993 on boards and committees including the World Bank's Committee on Governance and Administrative Matters. The only outside employer is the World Bank, an international body, so this is a public move; no private employer appears on the page.
records.source_title: Profile of the Governor (Bank of Guyana)

records.people: Kareem Michael (Monetary Economist from 2000, Deputy Director of Research from 2008, Deputy Governor from November 2017, Acting Governor from 13 August 2021, Governor from 1 December 2021)
records.move: from Deputy Director of the Research Department at the Central Bank of Belize to Senior Business Analyst at Belize Electricity Limited (2014) ; from Belize Electricity Limited back to the Central Bank of Belize as Deputy Governor (November 2017), Acting Governor (13 August 2021) and Governor (1 December 2021)
records.summary: The bank's own Office of the Governor page states the career as follows. He began at the Central Bank as Monetary Economist in 2000, led the development and oversight of the Bank's Statistical Unit, and was promoted to Deputy Director of the Research Department in 2008. In 2014 he resigned from the Central Bank to take up the position of Senior Business Analyst at Belize Electricity Limited. He returned to the Central Bank in November 2017 as Deputy Governor, overseeing the Financial System Supervision Department, the Research Department and the Compliance Unit. He served as Acting Governor from 13 August 2021 and assumed the substantive position of Governor on 1 December 2021. The outside employer is an electricity utility, not a financial firm, and the page does not say who owns Belize Electricity Limited, so the record does not establish a private-sector move; the central bank side of the career is the public side.

records.people: Jose de Lima Massano (Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, close to ten years between 2010 and 2023; Senior Minister in the President's office from June 2023)
records.move: from Executive Director at the state-owned BPC and chief executive of Banco BAI to Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola ; from Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola to Senior Minister in the President's office (June 2023)
records.summary: This speaker biography lists his roles as follows. He is a Senior Minister in the President's office, appointed in June 2023, and is described as the President's main economic adviser. He was Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, holding the position for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023. It also lists him as former CEO of Banco BAI, with no dates, and as Executive Director at the state-owned BPC, again with no dates. BPC is described on the page as state-owned. The page does not expand the initials BAI, does not say who owns it, and gives no dates for either banking role, so the record does not establish a private-sector employer; the publicly identified employers here are the central bank, the state-owned BPC and the Angolan government.
records.source_title: H.E. Mr. Jose de Lima Massano (Norwegian-African Business Summit 2025)

records.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia
records.people: Anita Angelovska Bezhoska (chief economist, then vice-governor, almost twelve years at the bank; Governor since May 2018)
records.move: from about eight years at North Macedonia's Ministry of Finance, latterly head of the Treasury Department and State Secretary in 2003 and 2004, to economist at the International Monetary Fund in Washington DC ; from the IMF to the National Bank, first as chief economist, then as vice-governor for monetary policy, research and statistics, and Governor from May 2018
records.summary: The central bank's own governor page sets out the career in order. She began at the Ministry of Finance as an expert associate on the financial system and spent about eight years there, heading the project to establish a treasury system and then managing the Treasury Department, and served as State Secretary in 2003 and 2004. She then worked at the International Monetary Fund in Washington DC for about two years, mainly as an economist in the European Department and briefly in the Fiscal Affairs Department, and since 2006 has worked as an expert on IMF technical assistance teams for European countries. She spent almost twelve years at the National Bank, first as chief economist and then as vice-governor overseeing monetary policy, research and statistics, and assumed the office of Governor in May 2018. The page gives no exact start and end dates for the IMF and Ministry of Finance roles. The only outside employers named are the IMF, an international body, and the national ministry, a government body; the page lists no private-sector employment.
records.source_title: Anita Angelovska Bezhoska, Governor (National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia)

notes:
Round 53, revolving-door row only. Six records filed, from six countries: BIH, SLE, GUY, BLZ, AGO, MKD. One record per person per source; no person appears twice.

FILED, WITH WHAT THE PAGE PUBLISHED.
BIH - read the CBBH's own profile page for Governor Jasmina Selimovic (cbbh.ba/Content/Read/119), reached from the bank's Governing Board and Management Structure page (cbbh.ba/Content/Read/15). It publishes a dated career list: Faculty of Economics Sarajevo since 2004, Fiscal Council advisory group 2011-2015, independent member of the Supervisory Board of Raiffeisen Bank BiH in 2018, president of the board of the Sarajevo Canton Institute of Health Insurance since 2021, CBBH Governing Board from 3 January 2024. The CBBH page does not characterise Raiffeisen Bank BiH, so one extra fetch went to the bank's own ownership page, which lists Raiffeisen SEE Region Holding GmbH as sole owner at 100.00% with no state shareholder; that establishes private ownership, so this is the one record filed with public_move false. The health insurance institute is a statutory public body and is named as such in the summary.
SLE - the Bank of Sierra Leone's own Board of Directors page (bsl.gov.sl/Board_of_Directors.html) publishes names, roles and appointment dates only, no employers, so it yields nothing on its own. The record comes instead from the George Washington University Africa Finance and Trade Initiative biography of Governor Ibrahim L. Stevens, which gives a full career: a decade at the Bank of England, Director of Research at the Bank of Sierra Leone 2008-2010 on secondment from the Bank of England, IGC at the London School of Economics, adviser to Rwanda's finance ministry on a GIZ-funded project, Deputy Governor July 2014, First Deputy Governor after the 2019 Act, Governor since November 2023. Every outside employer is public or academic, so public_move true.
GUY - the Bank of Guyana's own Profile of the Governor page gives Gobind Ganga's career with dates, including Director of Research 1995 to November 2003, Alternate Executive Director at the World Bank from November 2003, Deputy Governor from June 2005 and Governor from 2 December 2014. The World Bank is the only outside employer, so public_move true. Note the page is the bank's profile of Ganga; the site may not yet reflect any later governor.
BLZ - the Central Bank of Belize's own Office of the Governor page gives Kareem Michael's career with dates and names the one outside employer, Belize Electricity Limited, where he was Senior Business Analyst from 2014 before returning as Deputy Governor in November 2017. The page does not say who owns Belize Electricity Limited and it is an electricity utility, not a financial firm, so under the unstated-ownership rule it is filed with public_move true and the summary says so plainly. Both directions of the move are in the one record.
AGO - the Banco Nacional de Angola's own governor page (bna.ao/en/about-us/governor) could not be fetched; the site returns robots_disallowed. The record comes from the Norwegian-African Business Summit 2025 speaker biography, which states Governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola for close to ten years between 2010 and 2023, Senior Minister in the President's office from June 2023, former CEO of Banco BAI with no dates, and Executive Director at the state-owned BPC with no dates. BAI is not expanded and its ownership is not stated, so it is not filed as a private move; public_move true. A separate Ver Angola report of 19 August 2015 says BAI shareholders elected Massano to the board at an extraordinary general assembly on 18 August 2015, that he had held functions there before, and that he was expected to be elected chairman of the executive commission and to take office from 1 September 2015; it also does not say whether BAI is private, so it is mentioned here rather than filed, and it was not used as a second record for the same person.
MKD - the National Bank's own governor page gives Anita Angelovska Bezhoska's career: about eight years at the Ministry of Finance including head of Treasury and State Secretary in 2003 and 2004, about two years as an IMF economist in Washington DC, IMF technical assistance expert since 2006, almost twelve years at the National Bank as chief economist then vice-governor, Governor since May 2018. No private employer is named, so public_move true. The bank's separate CV PDF (nbrm.mk/content/Curriculum Vitae governor Angelovska-Bezhoska.pdf) returned a client error and could not be read; the HTML governor page carried the same career.

The International Growth Centre's profile of Governor Michael Atingi-Ego names only one previous employer, Executive Director of the Macroeconomics and Financial Management Institute of Eastern and Southern Africa (MEFMI) in Harare, with no dates, and does not mention the IMF at all. MEFMI is an intergovernmental institute of member states, not a private firm, and with no dates and no second employer the page did not support a usable record, so nothing was filed. Searches surfaced mainly Wikipedia and Ugandan news profiles; his IMF service is widely reported but was not on any official or employer page opened this round. Worth one fetch of the Bank of Uganda's management or board page next round.
KHM - searches for an official National Bank of Cambodia profile of Governor Chea Serey returned Wikipedia, a Bloomberg interview and a university speaker page, no career list on the bank's own site. Not pursued further and nothing filed; Cambodia remains open rather than confirmed blank.

His outside roles run through the Qatar Investment Authority, a sovereign wealth fund, which is a public body under the stated rules, and no page giving a dated career list was opened, so nothing was filed. If taken up next round, expect a public_move record.

NOT REACHED THIS ROUND, STILL BLANK.
No page was opened for BOL, COD, DOM, DZA, ECU, GIN, GMB, HND, IRQ, KGZ, NIC, OMN, SDN, SOM, SSD, STP, BRN, LAO, MMR, TON, VUT, SYC, LSO, SLV, BLR, CUB or TJK. The budget went on the countries whose central banks were most likely to publish a dated career list, and on establishing the ownership of the one private employer found. One process note for whoever runs the next round: constructed URLs are refused with a provenance error in this environment, which cost five attempts here. Every page has to be reached through a WebSearch result first, so budget one search per bank before the fetch.
